Re-reading Section 3:

"Only the first `\r\n\r\n` separates the header block from the binary body. All header-block line endings must be CRLF."

We did.

"The decoded request is at most 65536 bytes; the header block before the delimiter is at most 32768 bytes; each physical line is at most 8192 bytes excluding CRLF; at most 256 physical header lines follow the start line."

We apply. But note "each physical line is at most 8192 bytes excluding CRLF" — header block lines. Good.

"Header-block bytes other than CR/LF must be HTAB or ASCII 0x20 through 0x7e. Bare CR/LF, control bytes, DEL, and non-ASCII header bytes are errors."

We did.

"The start line is exactly `METHOD SP URI SP SIP/2.0`, with one ASCII space at each separator, method exactly `INVITE` or `MESSAGE`, and a SIP/SIPS URI from section 2 (not tel). No leading/trailing whitespace or preamble is allowed."

We did. But "No leading/trailing whitespace" — our split handles leading (gives empty first part -> len !=3). trailing (empty last part). Good.

"A new header line is `name OWS : value`, where OWS is any number of SP or HTAB and `name` is a nonempty SIP token."

We parse namepart = line[:ci], name=namepart.rstrip(' \t'). But what if namepart has leading whitespace? That would mean line begins with SP/HTAB -> continuation, handled earlier. So namepart no leading. But what if namepart is "  From"? Not possible because line begins with space -> continuation. Good.

"Here and below, a token is one or more characters whose entire alphabet is ASCII letters/digits and `-.!%*_+` plus backtick, apostrophe, and tilde."

We included set. Let me verify we included all: letters, digits, `-`, `.`, `!`, `%`, `*`, `_`, `+`, backtick, apostrophe, tilde. Our TOKEN_PAT: `[A-Za-z0-9.!%*_+`'~\-]`. Characters: A-Za-z0-9 . ! % * _ + ` ' ~ - . Yes all. Good. Note the order includes `'` and `` ` ``. Good.

"There is no whitespace inside `name`." We check.

"Names are case-insensitive." lower.

"A physical line beginning with SP or HTAB continues the previous header (never the start line); remove trailing SP/HTAB from the accumulated previous value and leading SP/HTAB from the continuation, and join them with one SP. Strip outer SP/HTAB from every completed field value. A continuation without a previous header is invalid. Empty values are allowed for ignored headers."

We did. "never the start line" - continuation can't apply to start line because start line handled separately and lines[1:] are headers; a first physical header line beginning with whitespace -> cur None -> syntax. Good.

"Normalize compact names f,t,i,l ... Each of these four fields and cseq must occur exactly once, counting compact aliases. Duplicate identical values are still duplicates." Good.

"Unknown headers ... no semantic effect beyond generic header syntax." good.

"Content-Length must be a nonempty string of ASCII decimal digits, at most 10 digits, with numeric value exactly the number of body bytes. Leading zeroes are allowed. There is no transfer coding, transport padding, or pipelined second request. Extra bytes after the stated body are a length error."

We did. But "Extra bytes after the stated body are a length error." This is same as content-length != len(body) when content-length < len(body). But what if content-length > len(body)? Also mismatch -> length. Good.

"All remaining recognized field grammar is checked before authentication or identity policy:" then bullet list.

"- From contains exactly one address, followed by exactly one `;tag=TOKEN`. Tag is case-sensitive and 1 to 32 characters. SP/HTAB may surround the semicolon and equals sign. The parameter name `tag` is case-insensitive. No other parameters are allowed."

We did. But "Tag is case-sensitive" — meaning value preserved case; our regex captures as-is, no lowering. Good. Length 1..32.

"- To contains exactly one SIP/SIPS address, with no header parameters. Its canonical URI must equal the canonical request URI. From may contain SIP, SIPS, or tel."

We did.

"- An address is either a bare URI, or `[display-name OWS] <URI>` with optional outer SP/HTAB and **no whitespace inside the angle brackets**. An absent display name is allowed. An unquoted display name is one or more tokens separated by one or more SP/HTAB. A quoted display name has outer double quotes and any sequence of SP, HTAB, or visible ASCII characters; an unescaped double quote closes it and a backslash escapes exactly the next visible ASCII character or HTAB. No bytes may follow its closing quote except SP/HTAB before `<`. Unmatched quotes/backslashes/brackets, nested brackets, comments, and trailing junk are invalid. Display names have no identity meaning."

We did mostly. One concern: "No bytes may follow its closing quote except SP/HTAB before `<`." Our validate checks rest after closing quote is only SP/HTAB. Good. But there's a subtle: For a quoted display name, after closing quote, the next non-OWS must be '<'. Since we call validate on namepart=s[:lt] (before '<'), rest is exactly the OWS before '<'. Checking rest only SP/HTAB ensures that. Good.

"Unmatched quotes/backslashes/brackets, nested brackets" — we handle unmatched quotes (closed<0), backslash at end (i+1>=n), brackets via count/inside. Nested brackets: inside contains '<' or '>' -> error; also multiple '<' -> find_opening_angle returns first; then gt; if there's a second '<' before gt it's in inside -> error; if second '<' after gt, gt != len-1 error. Good.

"- Call-ID is 1 to 64 characters from ASCII letters/digits and `-_.@`, case-sensitive." Good.

"- CSeq is `number WSP METHOD`, with one or more SP/HTAB, no other whitespace, number 1 to 2147483647 represented by at most 10 ASCII digits (leading zeroes allowed), and METHOD exactly matching the start-line method." Good.

"- PAI and PPI ... Split each row on commas outside quoted display names and angle brackets, then concatenate rows in arrival order. An empty item or empty row is invalid. Each item is an address, with no header parameters. For each header kind separately, the total is one or two addresses if that header occurs at all. Two addresses must be exactly one SIP/SIPS URI and one tel URI. Two identical URIs or a SIP+SIPS pair are invalid. These structural rules apply even to access PAI that will be discarded. Canonicalize and order each valid list with SIP/SIPS first and tel second. A single-item list keeps that item."

We did.

"- Privacy may occur in multiple rows. Split every row on `;`, strip SP/HTAB from each item, and lowercase it. Only `id` and `none` are supported. Empty items or any other token are invalid. Repeated identical tokens are allowed, but mixing `id` and `none` is invalid. The effective value is `id`, `none`, or `absent` when no Privacy header exists."

We did. Note "strip SP/HTAB from each item, and lowercase it". So token case-insensitive; we lower. Good.

Now Section 4 policy — re-read:

"The registry is the sole alias-to-account authority... Matching an alias uses canonical URI equality, never substring or user-only comparison." We use exact canonical membership.

"For an access peer:
1. If auth is null, reject with auth.
2. Syntactically valid incoming PAI is discarded completely...
3. If PPI occurs, every PPI URI must be an alias of the authenticated account; otherwise reject with identity. The selected identity is its first URI after the ordering rule, and the asserted list is that entire ordered PPI list.
4. Without PPI, select the account's default URI and use [default] as its asserted list."

We did.

"For a relay peer:
1. PPI must be absent and PAI must be present; otherwise reject with identity.
2. Every PAI URI must resolve to the same existing account, and that account must appear in the peer's allowed accounts; otherwise reject with identity.
3. Select the ordered PAI list's first URI, retain that whole list as the asserted list, and use its owner as the authenticated account."

We did.

"For either peer mode, the input From URI must either be any registered alias of that account, or be the reserved anonymous URI and Privacy must be id. Otherwise reject with identity. From need not equal the selected alias. Valid id is also allowed with an ordinary From alias."

We did.

"Produce a normalized outgoing projection: from is the anonymous URI when Privacy is id, otherwise it is the selected identity. Discard display names, PPI, and all incoming PAI spelling. pai is the ordered asserted list, except it is [] for external egress when Privacy is id or absent. An explicit none retains PAI even for external egress. Internal egress retains PAI for all three privacy states."

We did.
